Title: Q: When should I play these?

Messages.Author: Jonathan Cooper
Messages.Body:
My playgroup and I (somewhat all newbies) are unsure as to when to
play certain cards.. A couple examples are Claws of the Dead/Wolf Claws,
and Pulled fangs. Could someone help me out on this? As well, what sort
of guidelines should we use when determining when a card should be
played?

If it's not too much trouble, please e-mail me your response as well as
posting it here. I don't check the newsgroup all that often.

Thanx in advance.

jonathan

Messages.Author: Justin
Messages.Body:
In article <32B896...@interlog.com>, Jonathan Cooper
<dali...@interlog.com> writes

You play, and I think this is in Darkness Unveiled, Claws during Choose
Strike but before Resolve Strike.

Pulled Fangs can be played any time in the round after damage has been
resolved and you done more to them.
James Coupe.

To make it a bit more clear, the acting minion need not announce that they
are using their claws as they announce their strike. It is perfectly
within the rules to wait until the blocking minion's strike is announced
before declaring that claws will be used as long as the declaration is
made prior to resolving any strikes. Likewise, the blocking minion may
wait until the last moment before strike resolution to declare their
claws, though I don't know why they would need to wait.
And, yes, Darkness Unveiled is of little or no use as a guide for either
rules or strategy for Jyhad. Buy it for the cool cover if you must but
ignore what is inside.

Doug Dunaway
Follower of Santa

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
te...@lava.net (Alec Chang) writes:
>>Pulled Fangs can be played any time in the round after damage has been
>>resolved and you done more to them.

>I think this is the current ruling, although checking w/ L. Scott
>would probably be a wise idea.

Not quite - it cannot be played before additional strikes (if any).
It is played at the press step, or when the round ends (if it
ends before the press step - qhether by a vampiregoing to torpor or
by a S:CE).
